## PCA Principle Components Analysis

```{r baseball pca}

##Clean the data
baseball <- read.csv('/Users/meganyoumans/Desktop/Adelphi Coursework/Statistical Modeling/Datasets 2/baseballCSV.csv', sep = ".")
baseball <- read.csv('/Users/meganyoumans/Desktop/Adelphi Coursework/Statistical Modeling/Datasets 2/baseballCSV.csv', sep = "\t")
baseball$Franchise <- factor(baseball$Franchise)
nlevels(baseball$Franchise)
##29 
##set one color per team 
team_cols <- rainbow(nlevels(baseball$Franchise))

summary(baseball)
head(baseball)
str(baseball)

library(vegan)
library(MASS)
library(caret)
library(ggplot2)
library(factoextra)

```

## Including Plots

## https://www.r-bloggers.com/2026/06/pca-in-r-principal-component-analysis-step-by-step-prcomp-ggplot2/amp/ 

##Part 1 - predictor variables 

```{r baseball, echo=FALSE}

sapply(baseball, class)
num_vars <- c("Games", "Wins", "Losses", "Win.Loss.Percent", "Runs.Scored", "Runs.Allowed", "Home.Games", "Away.Games", "Home.Wins", "Home.Losss", "Away.Wins", "Away.Losses")
num <- baseball[, num_vars]
summary(num)
##show all the number amounts for each category at once 
colSums(is.na(baseball))
##check for no data

#checking correlations
cor_mat <- cor(num)
round(cor_mat, 2)
## rounds the numbers
heatmap(cor_mat, symm = TRUE, margins = c(7,7))
pairs(num[, c("Games", "Wins", "Runs.Scored", "Runs.Allowed", "Home.Wins", "Win.Loss.Percent")], col = team_cols[baseball$Franchise], pch = 20, main = "scatterplot matrix")
##very pretty 
##scatterplot looks very linear in associations escept for win loss percent

num <- baseball[, -1]
apply(num, 2, shapiro.test)
##all p-values are below 0.05 

##adjust the data set for PCA 

pca_test <- data.frame(
  logGames = log(baseball$Games), 
  WinPct = baseball$Wins / (baseball$Wins + baseball$Losses),
  RunsGame = baseball$Runs.Scored / baseball$Games,
  RunsAllowed = baseball$Runs.Allowed / baseball$Games,
  HomeWin = baseball$Home.Wins / baseball$Home.Games,
  AwayWin = baseball$Away.Wins / baseball$Away.Games, 
  AtHome = baseball$Home.Games / baseball$Games
)
rownames(pca_test) <- baseball$Franchise
str(pca_test)
round(cor(pca_test), 2)
apply(pca_test, 2, shapiro.test)

##p value above 0.05 for runs allowed, and at home games 

#Scale the data for PCA
data_scaled <- scale(pca_test)
summary(data_scaled)
head(data_scaled)

pca <- prcomp(pca_test, scale = TRUE)
summary(pca)

##Importance of components:
##                          PC1    PC2    PC3    PC4     PC5     PC6     PC7
##Standard deviation     1.8676 1.1568 0.9764 0.8683 0.61700 0.27057 0.11257
##Proportion of Variance 0.4983 0.1912 0.1362 0.1077 0.05438 0.01046 0.00181
##Cumulative Proportion  0.4983 0.6895 0.8256 0.9334 0.98773 0.99819 1.00000

pca$rotation ##rotate like the bottle analogy 

##Eigenvalues 

plot(pca$sdev^2, type = "b", xlab = "PCA", ylab = "Eigen", main = "Plot")
abline(h = 1, lty = 2, col = "blue")
fviz_eig(pca, addlabels = TRUE, barfill = "green", barcolor = "green", linecolor = "red", main = "Scree plot")
##that's really cool 
##Returns a standard ggplot object, can theme it using this method 

pve <- pca$sdev^2 / sum (pca$sdev^2)
cum_pve <- cumsum(pve)
plot(cum_pve, type = "b", xlab = "PC", ylab = "Cum Prop of Var")
## cumulative variance, things above 0.8 are good so 3, 4, 5, 6 and maybe 7? 

biplot(pca, scale = 0)
##uhh ok, fixing it next with ggplot2 

fviz_pca_biplot(pca, 
                geom.ind = c("point", "text"),
                col.ind = baseball$Franchise,
                palette = team_cols,
                col.var = "black",
                repel = TRUE,
                level.title = "Test") + theme_minimal() + theme(legend.position = "none")

##broken stick 

broken_stick <- function(P) {
sequence <- 1:P
divided <- 1/sequence
seq_sums <- sapply(sequence,FUN=function(k){
subset <- divided[k:P]
subset_sum <- sum(subset)
i <- subset_sum/P
return(i)
})
return(seq_sums)
}

P <- ncol(pca_test)
bs <- broken_stick(P)
round(bs, 3)

pve <- pca$sdev^2 / sum (pca$sdev^2)
round(pve, 3)


data.frame(PC = paste0("PC", 1:P),
           Observed = round(pve, 3),
           BrokenStick = round(bs, 3), 
           Eigenvalue = round(pca$sdev^2, 2),
           BeatsStick = pve > bs) 

##Plot 
plot(1:P, pve, type = "b,", pch=20, ylim = c(0, max(pve, bs)),
     xlab = "PC", ylab = "Prop Variance", 
     main = "Observed vs BS")
lines(1:P, bs, type = "b", pch = 1, lty = 2, col = "blue")
legend("topright", c("Observed", "BS"), col = c("black", "blue"), lty = c(1,2), pch = c(20,1))



## make a cutoff 
## Only PC1 beats the BS test and PC 2 is above eigenvalue 

n_keep <- 2
scores <- pca$x[, 1:n_keep]
team_cols <- rainbow(nrow(baseball))
pairs(scores, col = team_cols, pch = 19, main = "Retained PC")
round(pca$rotation[, 1:n_keep], 3)
summary(pca)$importance[, 1:n_keep]

##                            PC1      PC2
##Standard deviation     1.867629 1.156766
##Proportion of Variance 0.498290 0.191160
##Cumulative Proportion  0.498290 0.689450

fviz_contrib(pca, choice = "var", axes = 1)
fviz_contrib(pca, choice = "var", axes = 2)
##not sure here if we're looking to keep above or below the contributions line 


##Vegan NMDS 
##are teams similar to each other 

nmds_data <- scale(pca_test)
set.seed(42) 
## vegan NMDA needs a random seed set to start 
nmds <- metaMDS(nmds_data, distance = "euclidian", k= 2, trymax= 100, autotransform = FALSE, trace = FALSE)

nmds
##Dimensions: 2 
##Stress:     0.1118411 
##Stress type 1, weak ties
##Best solution was repeated 7 times in 20 tries
##The best solution was from try 1 (random start)
##Scaling: centring, PC rotation 
##Species: scores missing

nmds$stress
## [1] 0.1118411

stressplot(nmds, main = "Plot")
plot(nmds$points, type = "n", xlab = "NMDS1", ylab = "NMDS2", 
     main = paste0("NMDS (stress = ", round(nmds$stress, 3), ")"))
points(nmds$points, col = team_cols, pch = 19)
text(nmds$points, labels = baseball$Franchise, cex = 0.5, pos = 3)
fit <- envfit(nmds, pca_test, permutations = 999)
plot(fit, col = "green", cex = 0.7)
fit ##show vector numbers 
## there are some outlier numbers that are not near the vector lines, many teams are correlated to the log games area or btween log games nad runs allowed


## https://www.r-bloggers.com/2024/02/linear-discriminant-analysis-lda-in-r/ 
## https://rpubs.com/maulikpatel/229684 



## LDA test - assumes no colinear, predictors normal, similar covariance 
## where are the baseball teams best separaated from each other / division 

##have to make groups first 

East<- c("Baltimore.Orioles", "New.York.Yankees", "Tampa.Bay.Rays",
                "Toronto.Blue.Jays")
Central<- c("Chicago.White.Sox", "Cleveland.Indians", "Detroit.Tigers",
                "Kansas.City.Royals", "Minnesota.Twins")
West <- c("Los.Angeles.Angels.of.Anaheim", "Oakland.Athletics",
                "Seattle.Mariners", "Texas.Rangers")

baseball$Division <- ifelse(baseball$Franchise %in% East, "East",
                     ifelse(baseball$Franchise %in% Central, "Central",
                     ifelse(baseball$Franchise %in% West, "West", "NL")))
baseball$Division <- factor(baseball$Division)


table(baseball$Division)

##Central    East      NL    West 
##      5       4      16       4 

lda_df <- data.frame(pca_test[, c("logGames", "RunsGame", "RunsAllowed", "HomeWin", "AwayWin")], Division = baseball$Division)
round(cor(lda_df[, 1:5]), 2)


##            logGames RunsGame RunsAllowed HomeWin AwayWin
##logGames        1.00    -0.39        0.37   -0.33   -0.26
##RunsGame       -0.39     1.00       -0.03    0.48    0.37
##RunsAllowed     0.37    -0.03        1.00   -0.70   -0.60
##HomeWin        -0.33     0.48       -0.70    1.00    0.38
##AwayWin        -0.26     0.37       -0.60    0.38    1.00


lda_fit <- lda(Division ~ ., data= lda_df)  ## predict the division from every other column
lda_fit
lda_scores <- predict(lda_fit)$x

##Prior probabilities of groups:
##  Central      East        NL      West 
##0.1724138 0.1379310 0.5517241 0.1379310 

## plot the datafor L1 and L2 
div_cols <- c("red", "green", "blue", "yellow")
plot(lda_scores[, 1], lda_scores[, 2],
     col = div_cols[baseball$Division], pch = 20,
xlab = "LD1", ylab = "LD2", main = "LD1 vs LD2")
text(lda_scores[, 1], lda_scores[, 2], labels = baseball$Franchise, cex = 0.5, pos = 3)
legend("topright", levels(baseball$Division), col = div_cols, pch = 18, cex = 0.7)

##The teams are pretty split with NL only below 0 and the other divisions above 0 


```
